The game may have it's flaws but to me it's the most perfect thing in the whole world. We get these different characters and their contrasting personalities and we get to see them grow and go through hardships together, we get to see their friendship bloom and become a lifetime thing. I've been playing Final Fantasy when FF& came out on the playstation. Since then, I would say FF15 is one of my favourite FF games of all time.
There are a lot of good things going for this game, namely the characters: These guys are like real people and you develop a relationship with them somewhat. Not like some games where the characters are just tropes of other characters.
The scenery is absolutely beautiful, I was blown away when I visited the coasts and enjoy the long drives.
Your character is young but mature when he needs to be, which is great.... after all, you're playing as a King.

But as all games, it's not perfect.
The pacing of the story towards the end is too fast, you don't really have time to catch a breath.
It's a very sad story with a bitter sweet ending, very emotional. Wish they give more development in the ending to close off any loose ends.

All in all, still a very good game, dare I say, a masterpiece.
This is my opinion of the game. Hope it helps you guys out.

As details and little things accumalated, I grew attached to the plot; which even made me cry a lil at the end of the game.

So, overall, I really love this game for its depth despite superficial dullness (I only spent 30 hours and yet more hours to come). If you like a fast paced game, you'll have to find some time to spend into this game for you to like it.

Final Fantasy games have always gotten their fair share of love and hate from their fans. This game is no different. I personally love almost all of the Final Fantasy main franchise, except 13. And I didn't like 12 enough to actually play it, but I didn't hate it.

All that to say, I like FFXV. It has exactly the charm and beauty you expect from a main FF game. It certainly belongs among them, more so than 12 or 13 for sure. It is not perfect, though. A lot of the details of how the game wants you to play combat can be ignored if you simply warp strike constantly and just keep healing items around. I think this might be with a specific sword, though. The ability to stock up experience and then multiply it all by 3 by using the one Inn in the big city is a weird concept, too.

But, the point is that this game is fun. With all its imperfections, it's still a very fun game. I don't think it has the replayability of other FF games, but it's not a bad game. I think you will like this game if you liked FF7, FF8, FFX, and maybe FFXIV.

With FFXVI coming out, this game will probably be somewhat forgotten eventually if XVI is as good as it looks like it will be. But, it's there if you are interested. And I think it's worth the $20 or so.

A Journey of Brotherhood and Emotion

Final Fantasy 15 is far from perfect, with its share of bugs, story gaps, and repetitive combat. However, these flaws fade into insignificance against the backdrop of the game’s greatest strength: its characters and the emotional journey they take you on.

The heart of Final Fantasy 15 lies in the bonds formed between its characters. From the outset, you embark on a road trip with your best friends, your brothers. Every aspect of the game is designed to emphasize the importance of these relationships. Combat becomes a testament to teamwork, as you utilize each party member’s unique abilities. Camping at night isn’t just a mechanic for resting and leveling up; it’s a chance to witness your companions interacting and bonding, strengthening your connection to them.

The additional DLCs in the Windows Edition further enrich the stories of each party member, enhancing the overall narrative. By the end of the game, these characters aren’t just pixels on a screen; they’re your brothers, and saying farewell to them is a poignant experience.

Final Fantasy 15 may not be flawless, but it’s a masterpiece in its own right. It serves as a reminder of the profound impact a video game can have, leaving players with lasting memories and emotions that extend beyond the rolling credits. If you’re willing to overlook its imperfections, Final Fantasy 15 offers an unforgettable journey of camaraderie and emotion that few games can match.

I played this game at release to completion. It was a horrible game then and I have tried to play it for several hours and it is still horrible. The story is basically not there. I should be able to play a game and get a complete experience from the game alone. Other content can help but like FF7 the game needs to be complete and able to stand alone. The battle system is also kinda scuffed. It is just not fun. Worst of all the games. The attack system is dull and the warp strike over powered. Then there is the problem of a giant map with almost nothing to do. Barely and enemies and a bunch of kill these enemies quests. I know this game suffered in dev hell for a while and a bunch of ideas got through together to make this amalgamation of a mess but still I am shocked so many people enjoy this game so much. I was captured by two things in this game, the relationship between the main 4 characters and the unique fighting.

Everything else in this game just does not work. The amount of time it takes to travel, the sheer size and emptiness of the world, the lack of things to do, the lack of challenges and meaningful sidequests to face, the lack of extracurricular things to do of value, the weird hunter rank system which seemed to stall the game progression (likely because there barely was any), the clunky UI, the pedestrian driving (until the literal end game), the confusing, misguided, uninteresting, and short story. Throughout the game, I just mashed my buttons until I clumsily found my way through a fight, there doesn't appear to be much of a skill floor much less a ceiling.

It's a shame because I really liked the combat style. This is by no means a good game, but I love the idea that it could have been. The 4 main characters were nailed, their hobbies such as photography, cooking, and training. I wanted to explore all of them (especially the cooking). This incredible base was bogged down by the lazy mechanics surrounding it. If the actual story told was good and concise maybe it could have been saved.

TLDR: The game presents itself very well and the main 4 cast is perfect, but everything else sucks.
ignore the story and all the sidecharacters, these are the unfinished part of the game. Play the game for the chill roadtrip with the boys.

It’s surprising I haven’t reviewed Final Fantasy XV until now, considering how much I thoroughly enjoyed it and finished it back when it launched. This game delivered a powerful mix of nostalgia and emotional storytelling, anchored by the heartfelt bond between Noctis, Ignis, Prompto, and Gladiolus. Their journey felt genuine—both epic and personal—and the emotional weight of their brotherhood stuck with me long after the credits rolled.

The switch to real-time combat was a bold move for the franchise, and while it brought flashy, cinematic flair, my experience boiled down to relying heavily on Warp Striking with Noctis, which made combat feel more repetitive than refined. Still, the spectacle and world design kept things engaging.

Visually, the Windows Edition shines with high-res textures and smooth performance, making it the definitive way to experience the game. Playing it when it launched was incredibly satisfying. It’s bittersweet knowing I probably won’t return for a second playthrough, but the memories—of battles, brotherhood, and digital entrées—are still strong.

The emphasis the game puts on "Stasis", "Danger" and "Down" were never a problem in fights for me. Theres also no reason to spend time on Magic. With only 3 elements to use, I only ran into 1 boss fight where I was required to use Fire. I give this game a 7/10. I had a good time playing this game, I think I might have had higher expectations for it. If you want a newer take on JRPG's this is something to look into. If your looking to just get into the FF games I would recommend other games in the series first like FF 6,7,8,10.
